description:
src/cache.rs:592, 617, 774, 791 (and matching sync sites in crl.rs:85 / ocsp.rs:88): `CrlChecker::new(cached.bytes.as_slice(), self.inner.now_unix, self.inner.verifier.clone())`. The V: SignatureVerifier + Clone bound is propagated through the wrapper.

For verifiers that are zero-cost copies (DefaultVerifier, unit structs), this is free. For verifiers that carry state (a verifier wrapping a hardware key handle, or an Arc<dyn Verifier>), the clone is a refcount bump per check_revocation call. Not a real bottleneck.

But the design choice forces V: Clone on every consumer. A verifier that is naturally not Clone (e.g. holds an &mut to a hardware token) can't be used. Mitigations: (a) take &V in CrlChecker::new (changes pkix-revocation API; pre-1.0 fine), (b) accept Arc<dyn SignatureVerifier> as the canonical shape (breaks generic monomorphization, also fine), or (c) leave as-is and add a docstring note that Clone is required.

Out-of-scope for this crate to change pkix-revocation's CrlChecker::new signature; in-scope to note the implication and decide whether to push the change up to pkix-revocation as part of the 1.0 wave.
title: Every cache check on hit clones the verifier — V: Clone bound forces unnecessary allocation for verifiers carrying state
